name: Ranked majority
definition: If the same group of more than half of voters each ranks a candidate uniquely first, that candidate must win. This differs from head-to-head victories formed by different majorities.

name: Rated majority
definition: A candidate uniquely given the maximum permitted rating by more than half of voters must win. This is weaker than ranked majority for cardinal ballots. For ranked ballots use the first-place majority interpretation.

name: Majority loser
definition: A candidate ranked strictly last by more than half the electorate must not win.

name: Mutual majority
definition: If more than half the voters put every member of a set above every outsider, the winner must come from that set.

name: Condorcet winner
definition: A candidate preferred to each rival by a strict head-to-head majority must win. Different voters may form each majority.

name: Condorcet loser
definition: A candidate who loses every head-to-head majority comparison must not win.

name: Weak Pareto
definition: If everyone strictly prefers A to B, B must not win. For numeric ballots distinguish strictly larger submitted numbers from hidden preferences.

name: Strong Pareto
definition: If everyone weakly prefers A to B and someone strictly prefers A, B must not win. This equals weak Pareto on a domain of complete strict rankings.

name: Smith set
definition: The winner must lie in the smallest nonempty set whose members each strictly beat every outsider head-to-head. With tied pairwise contests, retain the full smallest strictly dominating set.

name: Smith independence
definition: Removing candidates outside the Smith set must leave the outcome within the Smith set unchanged. The definition assumes the same comparisons among retained candidates.

name: Independence of Pareto-dominated alternatives
definition: Adding or removing an alternative unanimously ranked below another must not change the outcome among the remaining alternatives.

name: Independence of irrelevant alternatives
definition: Adding or removing a nonwinning candidate must not change the winner among the others when their relative preferences stay fixed. For ratings, unchanged absolute scores are a separate assumption.

name: Local independence of irrelevant alternatives
definition: In a social ordering, deleting the top or bottom candidate must preserve the relative order of the remaining candidates. A winner-only API does not itself expose this ordering.

name: Independence of clones
definition: Replace a candidate with a group always adjacent in every ranking: outsiders should keep their winning status, and a winning original should be replaced by a winning group member.

name: Monotonicity
definition: Raising a winner in some ballots, with other comparisons unchanged, must not make that candidate lose. For a lottery compare winning probabilities.

name: Consistency / reinforcement
definition: If the same candidate uniquely wins two separate electorates, that candidate must win their union. For lotteries an extension compares common lottery outcomes instead of sampled winners.

name: Participation
definition: Joining with an honest ballot must not yield an outcome the new voter likes less than the result without that ballot. Ties and lotteries require an explicit preference extension.

name: Reversal symmetry
definition: If every strict ranking is reversed, a previous unique winner must not remain the unique winner. For ratings reverse the common numeric scale; lotteries require a probabilistic interpretation.

name: Homogeneity
definition: Replicating every ballot the same positive integer number of times must preserve the winner set or lottery distribution.

name: Polynomial counting time
definition: Can the winner be found in time polynomial in the candidate count and linear in the number of ballots, apart from tally arithmetic? This describes a rule and an algorithm, not the effect of a fixed demonstration cap.

name: Resolvability
definition: Under the usual large-electorate model, does the frequency of unresolved winner ties tend to zero? Deterministic tie-breaking or a fixed random seed alone does not establish this property.

name: Summability
definition: Can precinct summaries be added before counting the winner? State how the summary size grows with candidate count m; preserving all m! ranking types is very different from m candidate totals.

name: Later no harm
definition: Adding a lower preference must never harm a candidate already preferred above it. Completing the restricted ranked ballots accepted by this demo is not an available operation; the general rule is assessed.

name: Later no help
definition: Adding a lower preference must never help a candidate already preferred above it. This differs from later no harm.

name: No favorite betrayal
definition: A voter must never need to put somebody strictly above a sincere favorite to obtain a better outcome. Allowing an equal top grade is different from reversing two strict preferences.
